name: Senior Living & Childcare
summary: Family updates, tuition billing, caregiver scheduling, incident reports, and ratio compliance.

automations.title: Family Communication & Care Update System
automations.summary: Family members of residents receive an automated weekly update summarizing notable activities, wellness check-ins, and any care plan changes…
steps: Family members of residents receive an automated weekly update summarizing notable activities, wellness check-ins, and any care plan changes, keeping loved ones informed without requiring the care team to field individual phone calls.
When a significant health event occurs, the primary family contact is notified within the hour via text and email, with a follow-up call task assigned to the care coordinator.

Prospective residents and their families in the inquiry pipeline receive a nurture sequence with community highlights, pricing, and a tour invitation, filling the census pipeline while the admissions team focuses on tours and transitions.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a senior living administrator is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Senior living CRM or EHR (e.g., PointClickCare or MatrixCare)

automations.title: Parent Communication & Tuition Billing System
automations.summary: Parents receive automated daily updates from teachers via the parent app, and the center director's weekly newsletter is drafted from a simple form…
steps: Parents receive automated daily updates from teachers via the parent app, and the center director's weekly newsletter is drafted from a simple form the director fills out on Friday and sent automatically to all enrolled families.
Tuition invoices are generated and sent automatically on the first of each month, with late payment reminders sent at 7 and 14 days overdue.
When a spot opens on the waitlist, the next family is immediately notified with a 48-hour enrollment hold, filling vacancies without the director spending the morning on the phone.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a childcare center director has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Childcare management software (e.g., Brightwheel or Procare)

automations.title: Caregiver-Client Matching & Schedule Management System
automations.summary: When a new client is onboarded, this automation matches them to an available caregiver based on skills, certifications, availability, geographic…
steps: When a new client is onboarded, this automation matches them to an available caregiver based on skills, certifications, availability, geographic proximity, and client preferences, presenting the agency owner with a ranked shortlist rather than a manual search through a roster spreadsheet.
The confirmed schedule is immediately communicated to both the client family and the caregiver via text, and the caregiver receives a shift reminder 2 hours before each visit.
Missed clock-ins trigger an immediate alert to the scheduling manager so no client is ever left unattended without the office knowing.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a home care agency owner handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Home care scheduling software (e.g., ClearCare or AlayaCare)

automations.title: Behavioral Incident Log & Family Notification System
automations.summary: When a memory care team member documents a behavioral incident (agitation, wandering, a fall, or a significant mood change) the system immediately…
steps: When a memory care team member documents a behavioral incident (agitation, wandering, a fall, or a significant mood change) the system immediately logs it with timestamp, staff name, and details, notifies the memory care manager for clinical review, and sends an automatic family notification within two hours.
Follow-up documentation tasks are assigned for a 24-hour and 72-hour check-in, ensuring that no incident is documented once and forgotten.
The manager's incident report for state compliance is generated automatically at the end of each month from the logged entries, eliminating the manual compilation that typically consumes a full day.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a memory care manager handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Memory care EHR (e.g., PointClickCare or Eldermark)
Google Sheets or Airtable (incident log and monthly compliance report)

automations.title: Inquiry-to-Tour Booking & Enrollment Nurture System
automations.summary: Families who reach out via the website, Google, or social media are immediately enrolled in a nurture sequence, a warm welcome email with a center…
steps: Families who reach out via the website, Google, or social media are immediately enrolled in a nurture sequence, a warm welcome email with a center overview video, a text message from the director within the hour, and a self-scheduling link for a center tour.

Families who schedule a tour receive a preparation email with what to expect, and those who visit but don't enroll within two weeks receive a follow-up sequence highlighting availability, testimonials, and any current enrollment incentives.
The marketing manager tracks enrollment pipeline conversion rates on a live dashboard rather than piecing together data from three separate tools.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a childcare marketing manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: CRM (e.g., HubSpot or a childcare-specific CRM)
Google Sheets or Looker Studio (enrollment pipeline dashboard)

automations.title: Daily Family Update Digest
automations.summary: Throughout the day, caregivers log short notes on each resident or child, meals eaten, activities joined, nap times, and any mood observations…
steps: Throughout the day, caregivers log short notes on each resident or child, meals eaten, activities joined, nap times, and any mood observations, directly into the care app as part of their normal routine.

At a set time each evening, this automation compiles that day's entries for each individual into a short, warm, personalized update and sends it automatically to the family's preferred contact, no staff member spending 20 minutes at the end of a shift writing up 30 separate messages.
Families consistently rank this kind of daily visibility as one of the top reasons they trust a facility, and it happens without adding a single task to the care team's plate.
Any day with no notable entries logged still generates a simple "quiet, comfortable day" message so families never wonder if they were forgotten.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a resident care coordinator handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong.

automations.title: Medication Administration Reminder & Confirmation System
automations.summary: Tied directly to each resident's medication administration record, this automation sends the assigned caregiver a reminder at the exact time a dose…
steps: Tied directly to each resident's medication administration record, this automation sends the assigned caregiver a reminder at the exact time a dose is due, whether that's a 7 a.m. blood pressure medication or an as-needed pain management dose ordered by a physician.

The caregiver must tap a confirmation once the medication is administered, and if that confirmation doesn't come through within 15 minutes of the scheduled time, the director of nursing is alerted immediately so the miss can be caught and corrected before it becomes a pattern.
A daily medication compliance summary is compiled automatically for every shift, showing on-time administration rates by caregiver and by resident.
What used to rely entirely on a caregiver's memory during a busy shift now has a second set of eyes watching every dose.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a director of nursing spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Waitlist-to-Enrollment Nurture Sequence
automations.summary: Families who join a childcare or senior living waitlist are immediately enrolled in a periodic update sequence letting them know their approximate…
steps: Families who join a childcare or senior living waitlist are immediately enrolled in a periodic update sequence letting them know their approximate position and any changes to the expected timeline, keeping them warm instead of wondering if they've been forgotten for six months.

The moment a spot opens, whether from a graduation, a move, or a cancellation, this automation identifies the next eligible family on the list and sends them a notification with a 48-hour, time-limited link to confirm enrollment before the offer passes to the next family.
Confirmed families are automatically moved into the onboarding workflow, and the waitlist re-sorts itself without anyone manually updating a spreadsheet.
Facilities running this system typically fill an open spot within days instead of the weeks it used to take working the list by hand.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, an enrollment coordinator has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Incident Report & Family Notification Workflow
automations.summary: The moment a staff member logs any incident, a fall, a minor injury, a behavioral episode, this automation immediately alerts the affected resident…
steps: The moment a staff member logs any incident, a fall, a minor injury, a behavioral episode, this automation immediately alerts the affected resident or child's family with the relevant details and the specific next steps from the individual's care plan, so the family hears it from the facility within the hour rather than finding out secondhand.

A separate, parallel record is created for internal compliance purposes, timestamped, assigned an incident category, and routed to the compliance manager for review, entirely independent of the family-facing notification.
Incidents that meet a state reporting threshold automatically flag the compliance manager with the applicable regulatory deadline attached.
Families get faster, more consistent communication, and the facility gets a compliance trail that doesn't depend on someone remembering to file the paperwork later.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a compliance manager has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Staff-to-Resident Ratio Compliance Alert
automations.summary: As staff and residents (or children) check in and out through the facility's time-tracking system, this automation continuously calculates the…
steps: As staff and residents (or children) check in and out through the facility's time-tracking system, this automation continuously calculates the current staff-to-resident or staff-to-child ratio against the specific minimum required by the facility's state licensing.

The instant that ratio falls out of compliance, whether from an unplanned staff callout or a higher-than-expected number of children arriving before a shift change, the shift lead receives an immediate alert with the exact numbers and the deficit, giving them time to call in coverage before a licensing inspector or, worse, an incident exposes the gap.
A running log of every ratio dip, its duration, and how it was resolved is kept automatically for compliance documentation.
What used to be a manual headcount done every hour or two on a clipboard is now a live number the shift lead can trust.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a center operations manager, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
